content:
Sam H.: FYI hit sustained 92-96% GPU pool use in us-west from 08:11–08:26, low-priority traffic queued up and started timing out. I want to propose a graceful deprioritization playbook instead of hard rejects.
Priya N.: Curious — what's the goals? reduce tail rejects, keep high-tier latency, avoid thundering warmups?
Sam H.: Exactly. Goals: (1) avoid immediate 5xx for best-effort workloads, (2) preserve latency SLO for paid tiers, (3) keep cost stable by steering to cheaper paths (smaller models / cache).
infra-bot: alert: gpu_pool_us-west saturation=0.95 duration=900s affected_routes=[/chat,generations]
Jon C.: Sketch of behavior: when pool_util > threshold -> route incoming low-priority requests into a degradable path: first try prefix-KV cache; if miss, fall back to smaller model or truncate max_new_tokens. Only queue for short window (200-500ms). After that, return degraded response.
Jon C.: Example config snippet: ```json
{
  "admission": "adaptive_deprioritize",
  "threshold_util": 0.85,
  "soft_queue_ms": 300,
  "degrade": {
    "fallback_model": "redwood-small-8q",
    "reduce_max_new_tokens_pct": 50,
    "use_prefix_cache": true
  },
  "per_tenant_share": "weighted_fair",
  "max_concurrent_degraded": 200
}
```
Priya N.: How do we ensure fairness? if a noisy low-tier tenant floods us they could monopolize the degraded slots. Need per-tenant caps + backoff.
Miguel R.: +1 on per-tenant caps. Suggest token-bucket per-tenant and a shared degraded pool with min guarantees for paid tiers. Also track "degrade-count" in billing to avoid surprises.
Ava L.: Concern: degraded responses still cost GPU time. If fallback to small model off-GPU (CPU quantized) we save GPU cycles but add latency. We need experiments to measure unit-cost tradeoffs.
Jon C.: Proposed canary plan: 1) Deploy deprioritize admit controller in us-west on 5% of traffic (low-priority only). 2) Route degraded path to small-quantized model and enable KV-prefetch. 3) Collect metrics: p50/p95 latencies by tier, reject_rate, degraded_rate, GPU-util, cost_per_1000_tokens. 4) Roll forward to 25% if degrade_rate < 20% and paid-tier p95 increase < 10%.
Sam H.: Instrumentation checklist: tags on requests (priority, tenant_id, degraded=true/false, fallback_model), traces that show queue wait time and fallback decision, and alerts for per-tenant > 50% degraded.
Priya N.: Also add a quota burn notice to users: if tenant hits their best-effort quota we start rejecting instead of degrading. Prevents infinite backlog.
Miguel R.: AB test idea: compare two degrade strategies for identical low-priority traffic: A) short queue -> fallback_model, B) longer queue -> attempt full model. Measure quality delta (bert-sim on responses) vs cost.
Ava L.: If small-model quality falls below threshold we can attempt partial generation: return first N tokens from small model + best-effort async completion link. Might work for chat previews.
Sam H.: Action items: Jon to draft controller PR with config and metrics (ETA EOD). Miguel to sketch per-tenant token-bucket + billing tag. Priya to write the fairness rules doc. Ava to define quality thresholds and measurement harness. I'll schedule canary for Thu 11:00 PST and notify SRE oncall.
Jon C.: Will include simulator to replay yesterday's traffic spike so we can estimate degraded vs reject counts.
infra-bot: deploy-plan created by Jon C.: canary/us-west/5% scheduled Thu 11:00 PST
Sam H.: Thanks — keeping this thread as the playbook. We'll iterate after canary results. :thumbsup:
